value.rationale: An explicitly posed question on the validity of an arithmetic proxy for Fourier autocorrelation receives an exact counterexample. A sharp first common-aperture failure at length 21 and classification of the sole bad fiber are structurally motivated natural finite invariants, not a routine normalization test. The result prevents an incorrect reverse-product characterization of homometry; the negative claim is supported by an explicit factorization and exhaustive lower-range proof.
